summary.headline: Anup Engineering H1 FY27 hit by under-absorption; Q2 revenue ~182 crore, FY27 guided to 840-860 crore revenue and 120-128 crore EBITDA.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as disappointing, with weak revenue from low order booking in H1 FY26 and elevated raw material and shipping costs from the Middle East conflict. Q2 revenue was about 182 crore, up roughly 46% from Q1, while EBITDA margin was about 9.6% due to fixed-cost under-absorption. Pending order book stood at about 941 crore (vs 864 crore at 30 Sept), and management expects H2 revenue to ladder up with margins near 20% on Q4 execution. FY27 guidance is 840-860 crore revenue and 120-128 crore EBITDA (roughly 14-15% margin); FY28 growth target is about 20%.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Heat exchangers about 51%, vessels and reactors about 42%, silos and others about 7% of revenue. Oil and gas, petrochemicals and thermal power together about 80% of revenue.

segments.name: Technical services
segments.commentary: Repair, health-check and site fabrication business with three sites under execution, completion planned in H2. Target about 50 crore this year and about 200 crore in three years, at 30-40% margins.

segments.name: Mabel (Chennai, acquired)
segments.commentary: Acquired for southern geographic spread and silos/tanks capability. FY27 revenue expected at 65-70 crore, about 1.5x-1.6x FY26's 43 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of 840-860 crore and EBITDA of 120-128 crore (about 14-15% margin); based on current products and order book on hand.
Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin needed at about 20-22% to reach the guidance range, per the analyst's arithmetic which management accepted.
FY28 revenue growth target of about 20%.
Order intake expected at 250-300 crore per quarter given about 11-12 month order-to-delivery cycle and current capacity.
Expect to open FY28 (1 April 2027) with order book of 800-900 crore; target pending order book of 800-900 crore at any time.
Export share expected to return to about 50% over the next year, with about 30% of exports targeted from the US and focus on Nigeria and Kenya.
No new capacity capex planned for at least the next two years; Mabel also no capex for two years.
capex_capacity: Current capacity across three locations is about 20,000 metric tons per year, capable of about 1,200 crore revenue at optimal product mix.
Final capacity expansion (covering one bay at Theta) to be completed this quarter; no further capacity or capex planned for at least two years.
Pending order book of 800-900 crore considered sufficient to run the optimal-capacity revenue level given the 11-12 month cycle.
Technical services uses resources from existing capacity.
demand_pricing: Export share of H1 FY27 revenue about 49%; export share of current backlog about 33-34%.
Historical inquiry-to-order conversion 15-20%; management expects about 25% going forward with shift to complex and proprietary products.

Recent licensed/proprietary orders from Lummus (Netherlands, two products), TK Uhde (Germany) and LNT; each equipment value about 8-10 crore vs about 3 crore average today, with fewer competitors (about 2-3 globally).
Named domestic competitors in niche proprietary segment: L&T, Godrej and others; royalties are paid but applied to all competitors and built into costs.
Middle East about 30% of revenue historically; key customers Saudi Aramco and Rendering (as transcribed); contracts mostly FOB India.
New orders booked at improved margins versus H1 FY26 tariff-driven aggressive bids of about 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Exact order book and order intake for the quarter ended September?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending order book 864 crore at 30 Sept, 941 crore to date. FY27 order intake 597 crore to 30 Sept and 674 crore to date.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is letter of intent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 crore; LoIs are confirmed orders where work has started and PO follows in 2-3 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin jump to 14-15% for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 executed low-margin orders booked in FY26 at aggressive pricing to cover fixed costs. Orders booked in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 priced at improved margins with current raw material costs; Q4 execution margin expected 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ margin achievable and is shipping cost a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RM and cost escalation are built into the Q3-Q4 numbers; shipping remains uncertain but not expected to escalate much further.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East about 30% of revenue; contracts FOB India so Q1 impact was largely not logistics exposure. Focus on US (target about 30% of exports), Nigeria and Kenya.

qa_highlights.question: Inquiry conversion and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical conversion 15-20%, now targeting about 25%. Competitors in niche space include L&T, Godrej and others (three or four globally).

qa_highlights.question: Three to four year strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Move up value chain in proprietary/critical products; grow technical services to 200 crore; precision components (turbine machining job on shop floor); skid and package modules; selective acquisitions for technology and manufacturing presence (Middle East considered), not capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material risk mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Shifting to India sourcing where possible, vendor development in China and Europe for non-India items, and locking raw material prices quickly after order intake.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 revenue ladder-up and Q4 margin of about 20-22% must be delivered to hit FY27 guidance.
Shipping and raw material costs remain elevated; management said shipping is still uncertain.
Order intake pace needs to hold at 250-300 crore per quarter versus about 283 crore in Q2.
Export mix recovery to about 50% depends on geopolitical developments.
Royalty costs on licensed products and lower percentage margins on proprietary orders.
Capability-driven acquisitions being explored; no deal yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on forward order book and margin recovery, but candid that H1 was disappointing. Management was specific on numbers when pressed, though some answers (e.g., on the Middle East and shipping) were less precise.
key_quotes: I don't think we have ever had about 900 crores pending order books so that points to a healthy future, a strong H2, and on current trajectory a very strong financial year, 28.
So on an average start basis we will land up into 14 to 15% margin profile towards the end of the year.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pending order book rose to 941 crore (from 864 crore at 30 Sept) and H2 revenue is guided to ladder up, with FY27 revenue guided at 840-860 crore and FY28 growth target of about 20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no new capex for at least two years, with utilisation implied at roughly 70% (840-860 crore against a roughly 1,200 crore optimal-mix capacity), so no announcement is expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of 840-860 crore revenue and 120-128 crore EBITDA rests on a Q4 margin of 20-22% that has not yet been delivered, and H1 was described as disappointing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance needs Q4 EBITDA margin of about 20-22% against Q2's 9.6%, and shipping and raw material costs remain elevated with shipping still uncertain.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is moving up the value chain into proprietary and licensed products (recent Lummus, TK Uhde and LNT orders at about 8-10 crore each versus about 3 crore average), but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Order intake at 250-300 crore per quarter
rows.why: Q1 intake was about 310 crore and Q2 about 283 crore, and the pending order book is 941 crore against a target of 800-900 crore at any time.

rows.label: Improved margins on new orders vs H1 FY26 tariff-driven bids
rows.why: Orders booked in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 are priced at improved margins with current raw material costs, versus aggressive bids of about 250-300 crore in H1 FY26.

rows.label: Export share recovery to about 50%
rows.why: Export share was about 49% of H1 FY27 revenue and about 33-34% of the current backlog, with a target of about 30% of exports from the US and focus on Nigeria and Kenya, but this depends on geopolitical developments.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 941 crore order book and the H2 margin recovery to 20%+ but candid that H1 was disappointing; analysts pushed on the Q4 margin arithmetic (20-22% needed), shipping costs, and the Middle East exposure, where answers were less precise.
